### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via federationService (symbol, a top-level function), registerExternalDatasourceRoutes (symbol, a top-level function), external_catalog (literal, a string literal in a comment in registerExternalDatasourceRoutes; a string literal in registerExternalDatasourceRoutes))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via resolveExecutionContext (symbol, a field of interface ExternalDatasourceRoutesOptions))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via external_catalog (literal, a string literal in a comment in registerExternalDatasourceRoutes; a string literal in registerExternalDatasourceRoutes))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f3f09692589e7fab8bcb646468ec256e1468b365` — the merge of head `b5648f2fb463a1d4c70e8198d98fe3093711c5a4` into base `9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f3f09692589e7fab8bcb646468ec256e1468b365 && git checkout f3f09692589e7fab8bcb646468ec256e1468b365
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b b5648f2fb463a1d4c70e8198d98fe3093711c5a4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b && git merge --no-ff b5648f2fb463a1d4c70e8198d98fe3093711c5a4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b5648f2fb463a1d4c70e8198d98fe3093711c5a4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-core__src__meta-write-capability.ts.json, packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes-auth-guard.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/external-import-walled-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/admission-tenancy-posture.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts (`effectiveTenancyPosture`), packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`walledCatalogRefusal`, `resolveAnonymousFormTenancy`, `resolvePackageRouteExecutionContext`), packages/rest/src/direct-mount-composition.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/activation-gate.ts (`readEffectiveTenancyPosture`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md (D3, D11, D12 items 7–8)

Face: narrowing. `record-recognisers --paths` on the PR's twelve paths decides no face from the paths themselves (no governed path, no published schema) and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries the `(narrowing)` arm; so the floor is every path outside the prose faces (`.changeset/**` and `content/docs/**` are not reviewed), listed first above, and the cited code after the `+`. Net diff read at the merge base `9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b` with `origin/main`.

Check-runs on the head: 54, all completed, none queued. The ten required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Test Core` success, `Build Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Test UI` success, `Live E2E UI` success; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI` completed as skipped (the path filter, no `ui/` path in the diff). Also `Dogfood Regression Gate` success and `Check Changeset` success. The one PR comment is the advisory Docs Drift Check (see ③).

The rule reviewed against, verbatim from the seat post: "under the walled tenancy postures, importing a remote table as an object and refreshing a datasource's external catalog are catalog writes reserved to the platform operator, at REST and MCP." Governing text read: ADR-0131 D3 (the catalog is environment-level; under `group` / `isolated` tenant admins cannot create or edit catalog items), D11 (postures differ only in enforcement), D12 items 7–8 (one environment, one catalog; plants assign, plants do not define), and `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` on `main` (admits `isSystem` and the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung; inert for an absent or non-walling posture; judges every type alike).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, REST `POST …/external/tables/:remote/import`: narrowed, right.** `refuseFederationRequest` now takes a `catalogWrite` name; the import route names `'object'`, and after the family's capability rule the guard asks `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` with the posture in force, `authz.isSystem` and `authz.posture`. Under `group` / `isolated` a caller below the operator rung is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with the verdict's own sentence, before the `external-datasource` lookup. This is the rule, and the type named is the type the service saves (`persistObject` in `service-datasource/src/plugin.ts` saves an `object` through the metadata door's own save).
- **Accept set, REST `POST …/external/refresh-catalog`: narrowed, right.** Names `'external_catalog'`, the type `persistCatalog` registers (`service.register('external_catalog', …)`); `external_catalog` is a registered metadata type (`metadata-plugin.zod.ts`, `allowRuntimeCreate: true`), so the snapshot is a catalog item and the rule reaches it.
- **Accept set, MCP `import_object`: narrowed, right.** `federationService` takes the same `catalogWrite` name; the bridge's `importObject` passes `'object'`; the verdict reads `ec.isSystem` and `ec.posture` off the dispatcher's execution context, the same two fields the dispatcher's `/meta` save door reads (`meta.ts`). `list_remote_tables` passes no name and is not asked: it writes nothing. Right.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/rest`: one additive optional field.** `ExternalDatasourceRoutesOptions.resolveExecutionContext`'s resolved shape gains `posture?: unknown`. It is an input the registrar reads, optional, and the carrier of the narrowing above, not a capability handed to anyone; a host that passes none gets the verdict's refusal under a wall (the operator rung is the only thing that admits). Named here because it is the one exported-type change in the diff; it does not make the Clause-② spelling `widening`.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/metadata-core`: none.** Only the doc comment on `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` and the module header change; no new exported member, no signature change. The ADR anchor's invariant text is updated to name the three doors in the same sentence that names the others.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/runtime`: none.** `federationService` is module-private; `buildMcpBridge`'s shape is unchanged.
- **Unchanged, right:** the three read routes (`GET …/tables`, `POST …/tables/:remote/draft`, `POST …/validate`) still answer on the capability rule alone; `single` and a deployment with no `tenancy` service admit as before (the verdict returns `allowed` for an absent or non-walling posture, and the ledger test's stand-in now reports `tenancy` as not registered, so the import rows of that ledger still reach the service they read); the platform operator and `isSystem` are admitted under a wall.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/rest` patch, `@objectstack/runtime` patch, with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), the body stating that no key moves and nothing stored changes. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. That matches what the diff publishes: an accept-set narrowing under a walled posture, no schema change, no stored change; a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` with its banner, as the Post-Task Checklist spells it.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct spelling. The only exported-type change is the optional `posture` field named in ①, an input the narrowing needs, not a widening of any accept set or capability; nothing is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO migration is owed.
- `@objectstack/metadata-core` takes no changeset: its change is a doc comment and the anchor, no behaviour. Acceptable; `Check Changeset` is green on it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Acceptance note, "the rule sits at the doors, not in the shared save path": answered, accepted.** At the head, `importObject` is called by exactly two in-repo callers, the REST import route and the runtime MCP bridge (`mcp.ts`), and `refreshCatalog` by exactly one, the REST refresh route; the `@objectstack/client` method is a wire caller of that route. Both MCP transports reach the tool through `registerFederationTools` over the bridge `buildMcpBridge` builds (the HTTP dispatcher's `buildMcpBridge` and the domain's own), so there is one `federationService` behind `import_object`. The door-level rule is therefore complete for every caller that exists; the service contract still carries no caller, so a future door must ask the verdict itself. The verdict's doc comment and the ADR anchor now name the three doors, which is where the next author reads the list. No further action.
- **Acceptance note, the `PERMISSION_DENIED` code against the `/meta` door's grandfathered synonym: answered.** The family already answers `PERMISSION_DENIED` for a 403, the code is a standard member, and the sentence is the verdict's own (the tests compare it byte-for-byte with `walledCatalogWriteVerdict`'s message for the type written). Right.
- **Acceptance note, "breaking, patch": answered in ②.**
- **Docs Drift Check (advisory comment on the PR):** flags `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` (via `buildMcpBridge`) and `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx` (via the `resolveExecutionContext` field) as naming touched symbols, and `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx` as read-only. Prose, outside the reviewed faces; the lane may re-read the two pages. Not blocking.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` is the relay; the body's signature names this seat's session and the branch, which `Implemented-by:` records.
- **A sibling-family question is with the owner seat.** It concerns a door outside the rule under review (not the import, not the refresh, not this family), and it does not bear on this verdict; detail goes to the seat, not here.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts` — holds.** Ordering: `authGate` (ADR-0069) → anonymous floor → federation capability rule → walled verdict → service lookup. The verdict is asked after the capability rule, as the `/meta` save door asks it after `metaSaveVerdict`, and before any landing or remote schema is read; a refused caller learns the capability name or the posture, never whether the datasource or the service exists. The posture is read per request off the registrar's own `ctx` kernel, the kernel `externalService()` resolves from, so the posture judged and the service that writes come from one kernel. The async leg goes through `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture`, which answers `undefined` only for the registry's branded not-registered rejection and raises `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` for every other fault; the guard then answers that error's own `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, never a permit. Only a route that names `catalogWrite` pays the posture read, so the read routes keep answering under a tenancy outage. The operator is admitted by `authz.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`, and the resolver the registrar receives is `RestServer.resolvePackageRouteExecutionContext`, which is `resolveExecCtx`, the producer the `/meta` doors read; the envelope it assembles carries the ADR-0095 rung (`assemble-execution-context.ts`). `isSystem` is never set from the wire by that resolver. Tried to break it: no other route in this family saves a catalog item; the draft route answers a definition without saving it; the service's only writes are `persistObject` (behind `importObject`) and `persistCatalog` (behind `refreshCatalog`).
  - **should-fix (parity, low):** `tenancyPostureInForce`'s synchronous leg, taken only on a host whose `ctx` exposes no `getKernel().getServiceAsync`, wraps `ctx.getService('tenancy')` in a bare `catch` that returns `undefined`, so a synchronous fault that is not "not registered" is read as no posture. The `/meta` save door's `resolveAnonymousFormTenancy` classifies the same fault (`isServiceNotRegisteredError` → `undefined`, otherwise `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`), and so does `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` on the async leg. The production kernel takes the async leg (the booted dogfood pins prove it), and the stdio MCP door in `@objectstack/mcp` made the same documented choice for this leg, so this is a parity gap on a host shape no production composition uses, not a hole in the rule. Classify the synchronous fault with `isServiceNotRegisteredError` as the save door does.
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` — holds.** `federationService` asks the capability rule first (unchanged), then, when `catalogWrite` is named, reads the posture through `readEffectiveTenancyPosture`, the one read every walled door of the dispatcher uses (`meta.ts`, `packages.ts`, `automation.ts`, `permission-set-clone.ts`): `resolveServiceOrLoud` answers `undefined` for no `tenancy` service and the read raises `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` for a service that cannot answer, which the bridge surfaces as `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. The verdict reads `ec.isSystem` and `ec.posture`, the same fields `meta.ts` reads at its save door. So the MCP door reads the same verdict, the same posture source as the dispatcher's save door and the same caller fields as REST; the refusal carries the verdict's sentence with `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403, which the tool surface already maps. The listing stays a pure capability decision and the pair is listed where a call can pass it. Nothing else in the bridge writes a catalog item.
- **`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts` — holds.** Doc comment only: the roster of doors that ask the verdict now names the three doors beside the others, and the module header matches. No behaviour moves; the predicate still judges every type alike and no door pre-filters on the type.
  - **should-fix (cosmetic, low):** `WRITTEN_SUBJECT` has no row for `external_catalog`, so the refusal at the refresh door reads "Creating, changing or deleting a 'external_catalog' metadata item requires the platform operator…". The sentence is correct and is the one the save door would answer for that type, so the pin holds; a subject row such as "a datasource's cached catalog" would read as the other subjects do. Not a rule change.
- **`scripts/adr-anchors/packages__metadata-core__src__meta-write-capability.ts.json` — holds.** The invariant sentence names the three doors in the roster of doors that ask the one predicate; `check:adr-anchors` is inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- **`packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes-auth-guard.test.ts` — pins the rule.** For the import and the refresh alike: `group` and `isolated` refuse an administrator holding both federation capabilities with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` before the service lookup (the lookup list is asserted); the message equals the verdict's message for the type written; the capability rule still answers first (a `READ`-only caller is told the capability, not the posture); the listing is still served under a wall; the operator control, the `single` and no-`tenancy` controls, and the `503` outage arm. The mount is the real registrar over a resolver that states the rung, which is what the verdict reads.
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts` — pins the rule** at the bridge with the same cases (refusal under both postures before the lookup, verdict-sentence equality, listing served, operator control, `single` and no-`tenancy` controls, `503` on a failing `tenancy` service). The existing fixtures gain `resolveServiceOrLoud` answering `undefined`, the no-tenancy composition, so their pre-existing pins keep meaning what they meant.
- **`packages/rest/src/rest-write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts` — right.** The ledger's stand-in context now reports `tenancy` as not registered instead of rejecting, so the ledger's import rows still reach the federation service whose refusal sentence they read; a rejecting stand-in would otherwise have read as an outage.
- **`packages/qa/dogfood/test/external-import-walled-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` — pins the rule on a booted stack.** Under `group` (guarded: the `tenancy` service answers `group`, not degraded, and the administrator's rung is not `PLATFORM_ADMIN`): REST import, MCP `import_object` (a real agent token) and REST refresh are refused with the save door's status and sentence and nothing is saved or stored; the operator imports at both doors and refreshes under the same wall. Under `single` the same administrator imports at both doors and refreshes as before. The two must-hold behaviours the rule needs (refusal below the operator; the operator admitted) are both pinned end to end.

No must-fix. Two should-fixes, named above.
